question: pregnancy
note: Both agreeing sources give a narrow classical rule (forbidden in the sixth month of pregnancy), not a blanket ban. meandqi's wording closely matches American Dragon's, so it may be copied from it and the two may not be fully independent.

sources.name: Me & Qi (meandqi.com)
sources.says: Safety warning: 'Contraindicated during pregnancy'. Caution: 'Classical texts indicate this point is forbidden during the sixth month of pregnancy.'

sources.name: American Dragon (Dr Joel Penner)
sources.says: CONTRAINDICATIONS: 'This point is forbidden during the sixth month of pregnancy.'

sources.name: Yin Yang House
sources.says: Location, actions and Luo association only. No pregnancy caution.

sources.name: Attilio D'Alberto
sources.says: Location, actions, indications and needling. No pregnancy caution.

sources.name: Acupuncture.com
sources.says: Location, indications and needling. No pregnancy caution.

sources.name: TCMWiki
sources.says: Location, indications and method. No pregnancy caution.

sources.name: Atlas of Acupuncture Points (AcupunctureProducts.com, 2007, hosted on chiro.org)
sources.says: SI7 location only. No pregnancy caution. A search-engine summary claiming otherwise was wrong.

sources.name: Dynamic Chiropractic, Amaro, forbidden-points table
sources.says: SI7 is not in the forbidden-points list. The SI points listed are SI10, SI11 and SI18.

question: artery_at_point
note: The sources say the artery is close to or runs through the point region, not exactly under the point. A caution to press beside the pulse is consistent with them.

sources.name: Me & Qi (meandqi.com)
sources.says: 'This point is located close to the superficial temporal artery and auriculotemporal nerve... Avoid deep or aggressive needling.' Flags it as a 'Dangerous point - requires extra caution'.

sources.name: Chinese Acupuncture & Wellness (cnacupuncture.com)
sources.says: Regional anatomy: 'Vasculature: The superficial temporal artery. Innervation: The great auricular nerve and facial nerve.'

sources.name: A+ Medical Encyclopedia (a-hospital.com) entry for 听会穴
sources.says: Anatomy: '有颞浅动脉耳前支，深部为颈外动脉及面后静脉' (the anterior auricular branch of the superficial temporal artery is at the point, with the external carotid artery deeper); also '布有...颞浅动脉'.

sources.name: Yin Yang House
sources.says: Location and actions only. No anatomy or artery mention.

sources.name: Attilio D'Alberto
sources.says: Location and needling with mouth slightly open. No artery mention.

sources.name: Acupuncture.com
sources.says: Location and needling. No artery mention.

sources.name: TCMWiki
sources.says: Location and method. No artery mention.

sources.name: AcuMeridianPoints
sources.says: Location and indications. No artery mention.

sources.name: Atlas of Acupuncture Points (chiro.org PDF)
sources.says: Location only. No artery mention.

sources.name: Me & Qi (meandqi.com)
sources.says: Safety warning: 'Contraindicated during pregnancy (especially after the first trimester) as strong stimulation may affect the uterus.'

sources.name: Satyori
sources.says: Acupressure page, Contraindications & Cautions: 'Avoid during pregnancy.'

sources.name: TCMWiki
sources.says: 'Women with 3 month or over pregnancy cannot be punctured.'

sources.name: Dynamic Chiropractic, Amaro, forbidden-points table
sources.says: Lists 'ST 25 - Needle during pregnancy' as a forbidden stimulation.

sources.name: Acupuncture.com
sources.says: 'Do not moxa during pregnancy, according to the Prescriptions Worth a Thousand Gold.'

sources.name: Attilio D'Alberto
sources.says: 'Avoid deep needling during pregnancy.'

sources.name: Yin Yang House
sources.says: No pregnancy caution.

sources.name: Atlas of Acupuncture Points (chiro.org PDF)
sources.says: Location only. No pregnancy caution.

question: pregnancy
note: Only one source gives a soft caution, and none says to avoid the point. Attilio D'Alberto uses SP4 with PC6 for morning sickness.

sources.name: Me & Qi (meandqi.com)
sources.says: 'use with caution during pregnancy, especially with strong stimulation or sedation technique' (because of its Chong Mai effect on the uterus). This is a caution, not a contraindication.

sources.name: Attilio D'Alberto
sources.says: No pregnancy caution. Recommends SP4 with PC6 for morning sickness.

sources.name: Yin Yang House
sources.says: No pregnancy caution.

sources.name: Acupuncture.com
sources.says: No pregnancy caution. Lists retention of placenta and postpartum faintness among its indications.

sources.name: TCMWiki
sources.says: No pregnancy caution.

sources.name: Atlas of Acupuncture Points (chiro.org PDF)
sources.says: No pregnancy caution for SP4. The 'contraindicated in pregnancy' line in that section is for SP6.

sources.name: Dynamic Chiropractic, Amaro, forbidden-points table
sources.says: SP4 is not listed. The spleen points listed are SP2, SP6 and SP7.
